text: By the first orthogonality relation the irreducible characters form a basis of $\mathrm{Cl}(G)$, so the number of irreducible complex representations of $G$ equals the number of ___ of $G$.
explanation: The irreducible characters are orthonormal and span the class functions, whose dimension is the number of conjugacy classes; hence there are exactly that many irreducibles. This is also why a character table is square, with rows and columns both indexed by the conjugacy classes.
